acceptance: check_comment_policy.py allows new exception entries in quality/comment-policy.json when accompanied by new or modified files in the same change
Ratchet logic prevents re-adding exceptions to files in already completed scopes unless explicitly authorized
Test cases verify new exception addition in PR mode
context:
Discovered during PR #2773 and PR #2785 where uat-throughput-cedardb-nightly.yaml required a special test bypass because its lifecycle header exception could not be registered on develop in the same PR.

2026-10-09 tracker review: Dropped. Acceptance 1 (allow new exceptions in quality/comment-policy.json when the same change adds or modifies files) would let a PR authorize its own comment-policy exception without the required review, which weakens the policy. The scope (base-only exceptions) is absorbed by comment-policy-digest-and-base-exception-catch22-20261008, which keeps the review requirement. The CedarDB context (#2773, #2785) moved there.
description: In scripts/check_comment_policy.py (transition mode), newly added entries in quality/comment-policy.json exceptions are filtered out against baseline_policy['exceptions']. This creates a circular blocker when a pull request introduces a new file that legitimately requires an exception (e.g., UAT configs requiring mandatory comment headers per spec): the PR cannot pass the check because the exception is not yet in develop, and the exception cannot be added to develop without a PR.
